answer: A new name may spend only after it posts a 100-token lock for 30 days and gathers eight distinct counterparties on its first 30 settled receipts. Those receipts form a public work plume: a hash-linked list of job ids and counterparty keys. Established agents keep a crystal of accepted plumes and reject any applicant whose chain reuses a key or receipt already on file. Final admission takes three attestors with unlocked balances, convened as a small karst of reviewers whose votes stay on the record. Clone farms collide on the plume and never unlock the stake.
